scope: Corollary 5.1 (Canonical row–column sampling) of the manuscript “Polynomial removal fails for ordered binary matrices” (preprints/Polynomial-removal-fails-for-ordered-binary-matrices-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 190 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 120f7749fe55baa4), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix h ≥ 1 and an integer 0 ≤ q ≤ nh. Consider a tester that chooses a uniformly random q-element row set R ⊆ [nh] and, independently, a uniformly random q-element column set C ⊆ [nh]. It rejects only if the induced submatrix Ah[R, C], with the inherited orders, contains an ordered copy of H. Then Pr(reject on Ah) ≤ ϵh2−h q2 , and the rejection probability is zero when q < 66. For every fixed ρ ∈ (0, 1], rejection probability at least ρ requires q ≥ √ ρ ϵ −1/2 h 2h/2 , hence q ≥ exp(Ω(ϵ −1/2 h )) along the sequence ϵh as h → ∞. Here q is the sample size on each axis; the induced submatrix has q2 entries.
